$comment: The jobs that run on GitHub's included Actions minutes (CI-028, DOM-1079). The Enterprise plan includes GitHub-hosted minutes a month on a budget of $0, so nothing here may bill; the allowance lives only in dd-netcup-config etc/ci-hosted/valve.json. A job listed here uses runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_HOSTED || vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}; the organisation variable CI_RUNNER_HOSTED is set by the runner valve (dd-repo-registry bin/ci-runner-valve.mjs, which replaced dd-netcup-config alerts/ci-hosted-valve.py on dd-work-01): 'ubuntu-latest' only while the plan reads enterprise and usage is under 90% of the allowance, otherwise dd-ci-ephemeral. Add a row in the same change as the workflow edit, with the minutes a month measured on a 2-vCPU runner. repo is the repository name, workflow the file name under .github/workflows, job the job id. A row with runs_on pins one job to that GitHub-hosted label by name instead: only for a job that watches the self-hosted runners and so must never queue on them or on a variable it sets itself (the runner valve). CI-001 and CI-022 leave a pinned job alone and CI-028 holds it to the label; it needs a why and its minutes_a_month.

jobs.why: the runner valve points CI_RUNNER, CI_RUNNER_LIGHT, CI_RUNNER_DEPLOY and CI_RUNNER_HOSTED at GitHub-hosted runners while dd-ci-01 serves no jobs, and back when it does; on dd-ci-01 or on a variable it sets, it would stop when it is needed (DOM-1079, 6 Nov 2026)
jobs.measured: every 15 minutes, one job of under a minute, billed as 1 minute: 4 x 24 x 30
